text: Sentinel doesn't have its own separate automation engine. A Sentinel playbook is a real Azure Logic App, built and run inside the separate Azure Logic Apps service, with a connector that lets it read from and act on Sentinel. Everything you already know about Logic Apps — its visual designer, its run history, its per-execution pricing — applies directly here, because it's the same product.

Every Logic App, Sentinel playbook or not, is made of the same three pieces. A trigger is the one event that starts the workflow, and there's always exactly one, first in line. Connectors are pre-built integrations — to Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Microsoft Entra ID, Defender for Endpoint, hundreds more — that expose each system's triggers and actions to the designer. Actions are the steps that run after the trigger fires: send a message, call an API, update a record, branch on a condition.

That's exactly why a playbook's shape reads top to bottom, the trigger first and then a numbered sequence of actions. Here, the Microsoft Sentinel connector trigger fires when an incident is created or updated. Action one pulls the full incident details. Action two posts a message to the SOC's Teams channel. Action three adds a tag back on the incident. Each action names the connector it's calling, the same way a cmdlet's name tells you what it does before you've read the documentation.

The Microsoft Sentinel connector is built specifically for this job. Its trigger starts a run when an incident is created or updated. Its actions let that run get the incident's full details, update its severity, status, or owner, and add a comment or tag — writing straight back to the incident that started the whole thing, without an analyst touching it by hand.

A Sentinel playbook is a real Azure Logic App — trigger, connectors, actions — with the Microsoft Sentinel connector as the piece built to read and write incidents directly. Next: how an incident actually reaches that trigger in the first place, through a separate piece called an automation rule.
